what: Lucas down smash (AttackLw4 + AttackLw4Hold) donor material for Mythra c06/c07 (elight), replacing stock Mythra's down smash on those two costumes only

source.kind: offline extraction from the local 13.0.4 data.arc, read-only
source.method: tools/arc-extract (workspace tool) against gamedata/ssbu-13.0.4/data.arc, indexed by dumps/decoded/arc_files.tsv
source.why_not_live: the Snake up-tilt task could pull donor files live over arc-network because the console was on; this task did not assume a reachable console, and did not need one. Every input is in the local archive, so nothing here depends on the console being powered.

donor_acmd.why: dumps/scripts/ no longer carries SSBU-Dumped-Scripts-main (only ParamLabels.csv and gamewatch_motion_list.yml remain), and rule 17 forbids approximating a donor script. This is the same commit refs/brave_special_n/acmd_pin.json and tools/fetch_donor_acmd.py already pin, so no new source was introduced.
donor_acmd.files: donor_acmd/manifest.json (per-file sha256); lucas AttackLw4 (7087 B) and AttackLw4Charge (1618 B), plus elight's own two as the recipient control and robot AttackLw3 as the control for the dump's conversion errors
donor_acmd.tier: C - third-party decompiled text at a pinned commit

recipient_baseline.what: Mythra c06/c07 skeleton, idle and motion lists, pinned so this task measures against a known receiver
recipient_baseline.why_vanilla_skeleton: measured, not assumed: build_mythra_skin in src/pgwr/build.py copies only *.nutexb body/sword textures into fighter/elight/model/body/c06, and the 0.20.19 package ships no elight model.nusktb at all. So the body skeleton this port retargets onto is the vanilla one, and the audit asserts c06 == c07.

control.why: an independent dump of a *different* fighter's motion list, dumps/scripts/gamewatch_motion_list.yml, is compared field by field against what tools/audit_lucas_lw4_donor.py parses out of the G&W binary: attack_lw4 cancel 34, flags 0x80, game_attacklw4, c04attacklw4.nuanmb, and the hold entry named attack_lw4_hold with game_attacklw4charge. This is what proves the entry parser and the kind name, rather than leaving them to be believed.

key_findings.charge_kind: attack_lw4_hold (hash40 0xfee188235), NOT attack_lw4_charge. A first pass looking for attack_lw4_charge found nothing and read as a missing donor file. The kind and the script name are not a mechanical pair: kind attack_lw4_hold carries game_script game_attacklw4charge.
key_findings.motion_delta_is_two_bytes: Lucas attack_lw4 cancel 316 vs Mythra 56; the two entry bodies differ at byte offsets [62, 63] and nowhere else, and only the cancel u16. attack_lw4_hold is byte-identical between Lucas and Mythra, so it needs no change.
key_findings.bone_fit: 66 of 68 transform nodes survive on the Mythra skeleton, 2 dropped (Bat, BatL - his bat), 0 case-only matches, 0 parent mismatches. All 17 real limb bones present and moving; the donor clip has no Material group.
key_findings.havel_is_not_a_bone: neither Mythra's nor Lucas's model.nusktb has a bone named havel. It is the engine's built-in hand anchor, the same class of name as top, so the donor's effect anchors are used unchanged.

not_needed.config_json: none. Both clip file names already exist in the base game at the same ARC path, and ef_elight_c06/c07.eff are already declared under new-dir-files in the shipped config.json. The audit asserts both against the vanilla ARC index rather than assuming them.
not_needed.status_ids: attack_lw4 and attack_lw4_hold are vanilla status kinds, so no 0x1EE+ allocation is needed and Mythra's own status table (0x1F1.. for Hero's Spin) is untouched.
not_needed.sequence_sqb: the donor's down smash plays no PLAY_SEQUENCE record - measured by reading both pinned scripts - so nothing is appended to elight.sqb.
not_needed.articles: the only dropped nodes are Lucas's bat, and the donor scripts write no article and no work id, so this move needs no article at all.

not_established: Anything about how the move looks, sounds, or hits in game. Every number here is offline measurement (tier B) and a successful compile. The visual, audio and gameplay result is tier D until the user's console run.
